\begin{proof}
Let \(H\leq G\) satisfy \([G:H]=p\). The action of \(G\) by left multiplication on the set \(G/H\) of \(p\) cosets induces a homomorphism
\[
\varphi:G\longrightarrow S_p.
\]
Write \(K=\ker\varphi\). The kernel fixes every coset, hence in particular fixes the coset \(H\), so \(K\leq H\). Since \(G\) has order a power of \(p\), the image \(\varphi(G)\) also has order a power of \(p\). As \(\varphi(G)\leq S_p\), its order divides \(p!\); because \(p\) is prime, the only powers of \(p\) dividing \(p!\) are \(1\) and \(p\). Thus \([G:K]=|\varphi(G)|\) is either \(1\) or \(p\).

If \([G:K]=1\), then \(K=G\), and consequently \(H\) is fixed under conjugation by every element of \(G\); hence \(H\trianglelefteq G\). If \([G:K]=p\), then
\[
p=[G:K]=[G:H][H:K]=p[H:K],
\]
so \([H:K]=1\) and \(H=K\). Since kernels are normal, \(H\trianglelefteq G\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
Let \(H\leq G\) be a subgroup of index \(p\). Consider the permutation action of \(G\) on the \(p\)-element set \(G/H\) by left multiplication. Let
\[
\varphi:G\to S_p
\]
be the associated homomorphism, and put \(K=\ker\varphi\). Since every element of \(K\) fixes the coset \(H\), we have \(K\leq H\).

By the first isomorphism theorem, \([G:K]=|\varphi(G)|\). This is a power of \(p\), because \(G\) is a \(p\)-group. On the other hand, \(|\varphi(G)|\) divides \(|S_p|=p!\). The exponent of \(p\) in \(p!\) is exactly one, so \([G:K]\in\{1,p\}\).

If \([G:K]=p\), then
\[
p=[G:K]=[G:H][H:K]=p[H:K],
\]
which gives \(K=H\). Thus \(H\) is a kernel and is normal in \(G\). If \([G:K]=1\), then \(K=G\), so the coset action is trivial. In particular, every \(g\in G\) fixes the coset \(H\), meaning \(gHg^{-1}=H\); hence \(H\trianglelefteq G\). Therefore every subgroup of index \(p\) is normal.
\end{proof}

Because \(p\) is prime, \(p\) occurs with exponent one in \(p!\), and therefore \(|\varphi(G)|\) is either \(1\) or \(p\). Equivalently, \([G:K]\in\{1,p\}\).

If \([G:K]=p\), then the index formula gives
\[
p=[G:K]=[G:H][H:K]=p[H:K],
\]
so \(H=K\), and hence \(H\trianglelefteq G\). If \([G:K]=1\), then \(K=G\), so the action on \(G/H\) is trivial. Thus every \(g\in G\) fixes the coset \(H\), which is equivalent to \(gH=H\), or \(gHg^{-1}=H\). Hence \(H\trianglelefteq G\).

\end{proof}
